features.source: The Cherokee towns from before contact until the treaty of 1730, when the polity layer takes over the name. Drawn a little wider than the polity, over the Carolina and Georgia settlements that the political shape has to stop short of.

The same country from the Treaty of Paris, where the polity span ends, to the beginning of removal in May 1838. The gap between the two features is the Cherokee Nation's years as a polity — one ground, one name at a time.
